why: No search is needed: every digit of n is forbidden, so a same-length answer must already beat n at its first digit, and after that the rest can be the smallest allowed digit. If no allowed digit is bigger than n's first digit, take one more digit: smallest nonzero allowed digit followed by the smallest allowed digit. This is digit-by-digit construction; the week's backtracking label would also work but is overkill.
hints: List the allowed digits (those not in n). Can the answer share its first digit with n?

It cannot, since that digit is forbidden. So the answer either has the same length and a larger first digit, or has one more digit. In both cases, fill the remaining positions with the smallest allowed digit.

Same length: smallest allowed nonzero digit > n's first digit, then repeat the minimum allowed digit. Otherwise length + 1: smallest allowed nonzero digit, then the minimum allowed digit L times. Return -1 if allowed digits are empty or only 0, or if the result exceeds 2^31 - 1. O(digits).
pitfalls: If n uses all digits 1-9 (only 0 allowed) no positive number qualifies: return -1.
The leading digit cannot be 0 even if 0 is the smallest allowed digit.
Check the 32-bit limit on the final result, e.g. a 10-digit n can force an 11-digit answer.
